title: Sub-decisions: SQLite crate, Library::get return type, annotation intake mechanism
description:
Settle three open sub-decisions before coding begins. Record each as an ADR entry.

1. SQLite crate: rusqlite (sync, simple, no macro magic) vs sqlx (async, query macros, compile-time check). At M1 there is no async runtime in alcanzai-core; rusqlite is the strong lean. Confirm and log as ADR.

2. Library::get return type: the current trait signature returns Option<&KnowledgeObject> (a lifetime-bound reference). A SQLite-backed store cannot return a reference to data fetched on demand without an in-memory cache. Options:
   a. Change trait to return Option<KnowledgeObject> (owned — clean API, ~zero cost at personal-library scale).
   b. Keep reference return + add HashMap<KnowledgeObjectId, KnowledgeObject> cache loaded on SqliteLibrary::open().
   Lean: option (a) — owned return is simpler and consistent with how SQL stores work. This is a trait signature change; update library.rs before writing SqliteLibrary.

3. Annotation intake mechanism for M1: pure Rust binary (alcanzai-core bin target 'annotate') writes directly to SqliteLibrary. Python CLI wrapper in alcanzai-interaction deferred to M2+ when the interaction layer is more developed. Record as ADR noting the deferred Python wrapper.

Acceptance criterion: ADR.md has entries for all three. library.rs get() signature updated if option (a) chosen. Pre-commit green.
